candidates.excerpt: The GP20 was manufactured from November 1959 through April 1962. It was EMD’s first turbocharged, four-axle locomotive, providing an additional 200 horsepower compared to the GP18. Two hundred sixty units were built for eight railroads. candidates.title: Why the carrier with the shortest terminal wait isn’t always the fastest option
candidates.excerpt: Why the carrier with the shortest terminal wait isn’t always the fastest option Peak season volume has to land somewhere. The usual inputs to that decision are cost, space, and a general sense of which carrier “runs well” on a given route. Reliability gets discussed, but rarely checked against anything concrete, because container terminal performance data has not been easily compiled across carriers at the same set of ports. Here’s what happens once it is. The questions behind every port congestion decision A BCO deciding which carrier should absorb extra peak season volume is asking two distinct questions at once. 1. How often is this carrier delayed getting into berth at the ports I care about? 2. Once it’s alongside, how long does it take before the vessel sails again? Most routing conversations only ever look at the first question, usually filtered through reputation rather than a number.
